title: Jawboning the Fed: Do Markets Listen When Administrations Talk?
abstract: arXiv:2610.32300v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We provide the first systematic evidence on whether financial markets price political pressure on the Federal Reserve as a signal of future monetary policy. Using approximately four decades of Reuters newswire articles from 1988 to 2025, classified by an open-weight large language model ensemble into dovish and hawkish pressure, we estimate the daily response of interest rate expectations across the term structure, the US dollar, inflation compensation, and market volatility. Dovish pressure lowers near-term rate expectations by roughly one basis point per pressure event---equivalent to a four-percent increase in the implied probability of a rate cut at the next FOMC meeting---with the effect decaying monotonically and vanishing beyond the three-month horizon. translated_title: 口头施压美联储：当政府发声时，市场会听吗？
translated_abstract: 我们提供了首个系统性证据，研究金融市场是否将针对美联储的政治压力视为未来货币政策的信号并进行定价。我们利用1988年至2025年约四十年的路透社新闻快讯文章，通过开源权重大语言模型集成将其分类为鸽派和鹰派压力，并估计了利率预期在期限结构、美元、通胀补偿以及市场波动率方面的每日反应。结果显示，鸽派压力使每次压力事件下的近期利率预期下降约一个基点——相当于下一次FOMC会议降息的隐含概率提高4%——且该效应单调衰减，在三个月期限之外完全消失。鹰派压力则没有可检测到的影响。此外，即使排除特朗普总统任期，该估计也不会减弱，从而排除了结果仅局限于某一（届政府）时期的可能性。
tldr: 金融市场确实将政府对美联储的鸽派施压视为未来宽松货币政策的信号——每次鸽派施压事件使近期利率预期下降约一个基点（相当于下次FOMC会议降息概率提高4%），但鹰派施压没有可检测的影响，且该效应并非仅存在于特朗普时期。
en_tdlr: Financial markets price dovish political pressure on the Fed as a signal of future monetary easing—each dovish pressure event lowers near-term rate expectations by about one basis point (equivalent to a 4% increase in the implied probability of a rate cut at the next FOMC meeting)—while hawkish pressure has no detectable effect, and the result holds even excluding the Trump presidencies.
